pillar_reactions.evidence: Volunteered positive reactions repeatedly and tied them to his own goals: 'No, I think it really aligns', 'That's exactly what I'm looking for, honestly' on the teach-you-everything six-month framing, and at the end 'I love the breakout between the mobility and the, you know, the weight. And yeah, I think that's just awesome. That's exactly kind of what I was looking for.' He also welcomed the enforced rest days as solving a problem he had named — 'I feel guilty if I'm not doing something, so I'm horrible with the rest days. So this sounds like a really good structure to, like, force myself to take a couple days off a week.' He pre-qualified the coach against the whole category: 'I've seen a million of these guys on Instagram... him and there's only one other guy. They're the only two that have ever stuck out to me.'

Agreed without friction, largely because the rep validated what he already does — clean eating, non-processed food, and an eating window he had been running unknowingly for five or six years ('I didn't realize that I was basically sort of like intermittent fasting'). The one substantive point was the reverse of the usual: the rep told him he is under-eating rather than over-eating, at 100-120g of protein, and the prospect accepted it and supplied his own numbers. He agreed with the anti-snacking rationale and added 'I think I tamed that horse years ago.' No questions and no pushback.

Understood and agreed throughout — 'It has to fit your life', 'Awesome', 'Make sense. Right.' The rep had correctly identified this as his gap and said so. The only question raised during this pillar was about programme content rather than accountability mechanics: 'do you guys do any sort of like the pushup pull up dip type of stuff?' The rep confirmed bodyweight work is incorporated, which mattered to him because pull-ups are his favourite exercise and his climbing depends on them.

anchors.raw: Yeah, they're constantly raising my credit, and I'm not even asking for it. And they're like, hey, here's more money, just go spend it. But yeah, I'm debt-free too, so I think they want me to get that balance up a little bit. But no, think 6K is totally doable for me.
anchors.note: An 800 credit score, no debt, and an explicit statement that the full price is affordable. The strongest possible signal to ask for payment in full, and the rep instead recommended a 12-month external credit product at roughly $600 a month. This anchor was inverted rather than used.

anchors.raw: you can even spread it over 12 months. So that would be like probably $600-ish.
anchors.note: A rep-introduced anchor rather than a buyer-held one: $6,000 was reframed as $600 a month, which the prospect immediately adopted ('Yeah, that's probably what I'll end up doing'). It lowers the perceived price but raises the real one to roughly $7,200 and moves the transaction onto a third-party approval the rep cannot control — which is precisely what stopped the sale completing on this call.

anchors.raw: I have a gym on my first floor, and it's actually a really awesome gym. I wasn't expecting that, just from the pictures.
anchors.note: Free building gym, a 20lb kettlebell already in the apartment, and more kettlebells downstairs. Zero equipment friction and zero start-up cost, unusual in this corpus where most prospects need to buy a bell first. Combined with daily voluntary training, delivery risk on this deal is about as low as it gets.

anchors.raw: I've seen a million of these guys on Instagram, like we all have... him and there's only one other guy. They're the only two that have ever stuck out to me that I've ended up following... So that's why I ended up reaching out in the first place.
anchors.note: Third prospect in this batch to say the content did the selling before the call started. He had already been incorporating clips from the coach's feed into his own workouts. Consistent attribution signal across the batch: these are inbound, pre-sold buyers and the call's job is mechanical.

unmet_demand.want: An explanation for the sharp left hip pain that radiates to the top of his left foot — he raised it unprompted and openly does not know what it is
unmet_demand.why_unmet: There is no clinical or diagnostic layer in the offer and no clinician is involved. The pattern he describes — lateral hip pain referring distally to the dorsum of the foot — is not something a coaching programme can characterise, and nobody suggested he have it looked at. The rep folded it into the mobility pitch as a weak point Trevor would 'address', and then offered his own hip-dysplasia story in place of an answer.

unmet_demand.want: To learn how to plan and periodise his own training, which he named as the single biggest gap
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Actually well served and correctly claimed — 'after six months you won't need him anymore. You will know everything about kettlebells, how to structure a workout, and how to do it on your own' — and the prospect responded 'That's exactly what I'm looking for, honestly.' Recorded here only as a positive: this is the one demand in the batch where the offer and the want matched exactly and the rep said so.

unmet_demand.want: Grip and forearm strength specifically for climbing
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Asserted rather than established. The rep said it 'will just come naturally with just how kettlebells work' and pivoted to the longevity research, but nothing in the offer is scoped to climbing-specific grip endurance, and the prospect's stated problem is forearm endurance over a session rather than raw grip. Plausible but unverified, and he is buying partly on it.
